Main primitive: K supplied elements in an effective finite group (not necessarily abelian), fixed unknown common annihilator h in given positive integer interval [Hlo,Hhi], W=width. Maintain L=1 dividing every possible common h. Set a=ceil(Hlo/L),z=floor(Hhi/L),w=z-a. If singleton return L*a. For each g, beta=g^L; if beta=1 mark done at powering cost. Otherwise exact bounded-order search<=w; small r>=2 yields L*=r (which divides h), annihilating g and retaining previous annihilations; large order>w means interval BSGS gives unique k with beta^k=1, hence h=Lk. If all elements consumed, output common annihilator L (may be <group cardinality). Each nontrivial search either doubles L or terminates, so sum sqrt(w)<=O(sqrt W), while no-growth elements skip BSGS. Proposed total soft bit/group envelope O~((K+sqrt W+1)*poly(logHhi)) with actual group operation encodings/equality, exponentiation, shifts, sorting and integer widths paid.
